prompt.text:
Lets do some investigation.

Goal: find all potentially reusable code and document it

Workflow (do in micro-iterations):

1. Iterate over every golang file except tests
2. For each file:
   2.1 Analyze function
   2.2 Ask yourself question: is it reusable?
       Criterie:
       a) it is doing something, that possibly could be done in other packages if we generalize function
       b) it is already generic, to make it fully generic we just have to rewrite it with generics
       c) it could be decomposed in generic functions
       d) it could be removed at all if other known function from specs/ref/LIST.md will be used
   2.3 Take action:
       if a,b,c - document into specs/ref/LIST.md
       if d - add info into specs/ref/LIST.md near corresponding function that could be used
       
3. Read specs/ref/LIST.md
   3.1 Read it
   3.2 Start writing specs/ref/SPEC.md
   3.3 Spec should have organized clusters of functions. They should be organized around problem domain

LIST.md format:
```

## Dedup opportunities

1. {path/to/package}
   
   Function: {function name}
   Position: {position in code}
   Findings: {What did you find during analysis}
   Could replace:
     { list of functions from other packages per 2.2d)
     - path/to/package:999:99:FuncitonName 
     ...
...
```

Track your progress as graph

```
[ {pkg1} [x] ] -> [ {pkg2} [✅] ] -> [ {pkg2.1} [🚫] ]
                                 -> [ {pkg2.2} [🚫] ]
               -> [ {pkg3} [⌛] ] ->  [ {pkg3} [ ] ]
```

Graph help you navigate your thought. always do one movement at a time in graph

Legend:
✅ - Done, completed, or checked hypothesis
🚫 - Canceled
⌛ - next, current work
[ ] - not complete, not checked

REMEMBER DOING MICRO-LOOPS, FREQUENTLY UPDATING LIST.MD
